# Rebased Review

Rebased shows a per-line gutter "add comment" affordance and a visible inline
comment (like a GitHub/GitLab PR review, not just a gutter marker) on any
diff of a local/uncommitted change -- double-click a changed file in Local
Changes, or "Show Diff". No dedicated action is needed to start reviewing;
comments accumulate in a project-wide store as the user opens diffs. Clicking
"Finish Review" in the Local Changes toolbar exports every accumulated
comment to a JSON file and clears the store.

This skill drives that loop from the agent side: make sure Rebased is open on
the project, tell the user to review and click "Finish Review", wait for the
export, read the comments, plan and apply fixes, then loop back so the user
can verify and leave more.

There is also a `review` CLI command (`rebased review [<ref>]`) that opens a
dedicated multi-file diff session for a whole changeset from a terminal, with
its own "Finish Review" action that also closes the window it's blocking on
-- useful for scripting/automation, but **only produces visible comments
when a project is already open** in some running Rebased instance (it falls
back to a window mode that silently can't show the comment UI otherwise).
Prefer the primary flow below; only reach for the CLI command if the user
explicitly asks to run it from a terminal.

## Activation triggers

- "diff review"
- "review my changes"
- "review this with rebased"
- (proactively, after finishing a meaningful chunk of code changes, if the
  user's workflow with this skill has been established in the conversation)

## Workflow

### 0. Check there's actually something to review

```bash
git -C "<repo-root>" status --porcelain
```

If this is empty (clean working tree, no uncommitted changes), there is
nothing for a local-changes diff to show — stop here and tell the user
there's nothing to review, rather than launching Rebased or waiting on a
comment export that can never come from an empty Local Changes view.

### 1. Determine the repo root and clear stale state

```bash
git -C . rev-parse --show-toplevel
```

Delete any pre-existing export at both possible paths before waiting, so a
stale file from an earlier/interrupted round is never mistaken for this
round's output:

```bash
rm -f "<repo-root>/.git/review-comments.json" "<repo-root>/.git-review-comments.json"
```

(The second path is the worktree/submodule fallback -- see step 3.)

### 2. Make sure Rebased is open on the project

Check whether Rebased is already running:

```bash
pgrep -f "Rebased.app/Contents/MacOS/rebased"
```

- If it's already running, assume the user is already looking at (or can
  switch to) that window -- do not launch a second instance, and remember
  this skill did **not** launch it (so step 6/7 must not close it later).
- If not running, launch it pointed at the repo root so it opens as a
  project (matching the `idea .`-style convention -- passing `.` opens the
  current working directory), and remember that this skill **did** launch
  it, for the same reason:

  ```bash
  rebased "<repo-root>" &
  ```

  If `rebased` isn't on `PATH` (not installed via the Homebrew tap), fall
  back to `/Applications/Rebased.app/Contents/MacOS/rebased`, or tell the
  user to launch it manually if neither is found.

Tell the user plainly: describe what changed, then ask them to open the
diff (Local Changes → double-click a changed file, or "Show Diff"), leave
comments, and click "Finish Review" in the Local Changes toolbar when done.

### 3. Wait for the export, but only act if there's something to act on

Poll for the JSON file rather than blocking on a process (there is no
blocking CLI call in this flow -- the app stays open independently):

```bash
until [ -s "<repo-root>/.git/review-comments.json" ] || [ -s "<repo-root>/.git-review-comments.json" ]; do
  sleep 5
done
```

Run this as one foreground Bash call with a generous timeout (the user is
actively reviewing) rather than scheduling a separate background wakeup.

Once a file appears with content, read it. Each entry has the shape:

```json
{ "filePath": "path/relative/to/repo/root", "line": 1, "side": "LEFT", "text": "comment text" }
```

`side` is `"LEFT"` (old/before content) or `"RIGHT"` (new/after content).
`line` is 1-based.

- If the exported array is **empty** (`[]`) — the user clicked "Finish
  Review" with nothing to flag. Treat this as "review complete, no
  outstanding comments" — apply the same close-the-app-if-this-skill-
  launched-it step described at the end of step 6, then stop and tell the
  user so.
- If it has entries, continue to step 4. Only start planning/iterating once
  there is at least one real comment to act on — an empty export is a
  legitimate "done" signal, not a bug.

### 4. Plan the fixes

Format each `{filePath, line, side, text}` entry as a `file:line` annotation,
noting the side (`LEFT` = comment refers to the old content at that line,
`RIGHT` = the new content). For example:

```
plugins/foo/src/Bar.kt:42 (RIGHT) — "this should use the existing helper instead"
```

Enter plan mode, list every annotation together with the intended fix, and
get the user's approval before touching any files.

### 5. Apply the fixes

Once approved, apply the fixes to the real source files.

### 6. Ask before looping — don't just poll again silently

The "Finish Review" button requires at least one comment to be clickable
(deliberately — a stray click with nothing to say shouldn't produce a fake
"done" signal), so **do not** silently re-enter the polling loop after
applying fixes: if the user has nothing further to flag, they have no way to
signal that back through the button, and the poll would hang forever with no
way out.

Instead, ask directly: "Fixes applied. Want another round of review, or is
this good?"

- If the user wants another round: delete the export file(s) again (same
  command as step 1), remind them the fixes are in and Rebased is still open
  for them to re-review, then repeat step 3 (poll again).
- If the user says they're done (in any form — "looks good", "done", "no"):
  stop polling. If this skill launched Rebased itself in step 2 (not if it
  was already running before), close it gracefully:

  ```bash
  osascript -e 'tell application "Rebased" to quit'
  ```

  (a graceful quit, not a force-kill, so the app can handle any of its own
  shutdown/save state normally). Never close it if it was already running
  before this skill started — that instance isn't this skill's to manage.
  Then tell the user the review is complete.

### 7. Loop until done

Repeat steps 3–6 until either a round comes back with an empty array, or the
user says they're done in step 6. Either way, tell the user the review is
complete.

## Using the `review` CLI command instead

If the user explicitly asks to drive this from a terminal:

```bash
rebased review [<ref>]
```

takes zero or one optional ref argument (no argument = uncommitted changes;
a single ref or a range like `main..feature`/`main...feature` = that
comparison). This call **blocks until the reviewer closes the review
window** — run it as a normal foreground command with a generous timeout,
not backgrounded. It clears and re-exports the same
`<repo-root>/.git/review-comments.json` file on its own "Finish Review"
click, so steps 3–5 above still apply once it returns; only skip the polling
loop in step 3 since the process return is itself the completion signal.
Remind the user this path only shows the comment UI if a project is already
open in some other running Rebased instance.
